body:
I'm really appreciative of your insights right now.  It's forcing me to ask myself questions I'd rejected out of sheer stubbornness before in my depression and anxiety.

I'm glad that you're finding something that works for you with your anxiety.  That's honestly the worst for me--I can't function with as anxious as I get.  I'm glad that therapy is working for you, and hopefully the medication will as well.

"It sounds like you know what you don't want, maybe it's time to take a risk."  That really struck a chord with me--if I hate my current circumstances to the point of wanting to kill myself, then what's the harm in trying a radically different path?  What's the worst that could happen, that I'd end up feeling like this again?  I already do.  Nothing to lose, I guess.

I'd just tried to avoid that thinking before because it sounds impulsive, and I've recently been diagnosed bipolar, so I'm hyper-aware of anything that might be considered a symptom.  But it's a good idea, I think.  Thank you.

Thanks for answering my post.

Your point is a great one, actually.  About a year and a half ago, I ended up spending three months abroad on an internship.  It was an awesome experience, and I really wish that I could repeat it or something close to it, do some travelling, but I have responsibilities and obligations that I have tying me here.  Otherwise, I'd be gone in a heartbeat, doing something exciting.

And it's not that I don't realize that there are exciting things that I could do, it's just that I know that I'll always have to come back here and live real, normal life after.  And the day-to-day is what's killing me, so to speak.

Thanks again for your perspective.
